mainTopic: Slaves' immersion for freedom, owning the body versus the work, the rulings in גבלא, and what makes a גר
overview: The amud opens by explaining why a slave that a ישראל bought from a גוי can free himself by immersing for freedom. The גוי owned only the slave's work, not his body, so that is all the ישראל bought, and רבא's rule says שחרור cancels such a claim. רב חסדא challenges this from the story of בלוריא הגיורת, and רבא answers that after the owner converts, only an immersion done explicitly for freedom works. רב אַוְיָא says a גוי who sells himself is acquired body and all, learning it from 'מהם תקנו', but רב אחא's challenge to him is left as a קשיא. שמואל rules that the owner must hold the slave firmly in the water, and the story of רב אשי's slave shows how this was done. רבא answers רב פפא that people enslaved for an unpaid head-tax are real slaves, based on רב ששת's teaching about the king. In the story of גבלא, רבי יוחנן orders announcements about ממזרים, יין נסך and בישולי גוים, and the גמרא explains each one. Finally a ברייתא records three views on what makes a גר: מילה alone, טבילה alone, or both. The גמרא asks why each תנא uses only one source, rejects the answer 'אין דנין אפשר משאי אפשר', and begins a new answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A gentile owner never owned the slave's body
steps.stepSummary: A גוי owns only the slave's work, not his body. So that is all a ישראל can buy from him, and the slave's immersion for freedom cancels that claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: A gentile does not own the slave's body. Only what he owns can he sell to a Jew. So once the slave got ahead and immersed to become free, he cancelled his master's claim on his work.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a slave bought from a גוי goes free when he immerses on his own to become a בן חורין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key idea is that a גוי cannot own another person's body (קנין הגוף). He has only a claim on the slave's work (שעבוד). The ישראל who buys the slave gets only that same weaker claim, and a weak claim like that can be cancelled when the slave immerses to become free.

keyTerms.meaning: The body itself, meaning full ownership of the person
Transfers ownership to someone else
Got ahead, acted first
A free man
He cancelled it, removed it
A claim or lien, here the right to the slave's work

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the slave simply walked away from his owner. The point is that the owner never had more than a claim on his work, and that kind of claim can be cancelled.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between owning the body and owning only the work runs through the rest of this discussion.

phrases.english: A gentile does not acquire the slave's body;
what he does acquire in him
is what he transfers to the Jew,
and since he got ahead and immersed
for the sake of being a free man
he cancelled the claim on him.
phrases.notes: The claim here is the master's right to the slave's work.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹי גּוּפָא לָא קָנֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion by explaining why a slave bought from a גוי can free himself through immersion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Conceptual distinction between owning the body and owning only a claim on the work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a ישראל owner fully owns the slave, so the slave's immersion should not free him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ישראל bought only what the גוי had, a work-claim, and immersion for freedom cancels it.

steps.title: This fits רבא's rule that certain things erase a lien
steps.stepSummary: The explanation matches רבא's rule that הקדש, חמץ and שחרור cancel any שעבוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבא, who said: consecrating something, the prohibition of חמץ, and freeing a slave all remove a lien.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the explanation by pointing to a general rule of רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא teaches that some powerful changes in status wipe out any claim (שעבוד) that someone had on an item. Freeing a slave (שחרור) is one of them. So the slave's immersion for freedom can cancel the owner's work-claim.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrating an item to the בית המקדש
Leavened food, forbidden on פסח
Freeing a slave
They cancel, remove

phrases.english: This is like Rava, for Rava said:
Consecration, chametz, and freeing a slave
remove an item from a lien.
phrases.notes: With חמץ, he means the moment the פסח prohibition falls on the food.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 by linking it to a known general rule.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 1 that immersion for freedom cancels the owner's work-claim
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's rule: הקדש, חמץ ושחרור מפקיעין מידי שעבוד

steps.title: רב חסדא's challenge from the story of בלוריא
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא brings a ברייתא: בלוריא's slaves immersed before her and went free. That suggests that after her conversion they would not go free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא objected: there was a case with בלוריא the convert, whose slaves got ahead and immersed before she did. The case came to the חכמים, and they said the slaves acquired themselves as free men. That implies: before her, yes; after her, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא challenges the explanation using a story about a convert whose slaves immersed before her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stresses that the slaves immersed "before her." רב חסדא reads this to mean that if they had immersed after she converted, they would not have gone free. That seems to clash with step 1, which said a work-claim like this can be cancelled by immersing for freedom.

keyTerms.meaning: A female convert
Before her
After her

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says "after her, no." רב חסדא is reading that from the fact that the ברייתא says "before her."

phrases.english: Rav Chisda raised an objection:
There was an incident with Beloreya the convert
whose slaves got ahead and immersed before her,
and the incident came before the Sages,
and they said: they acquired themselves as free men.
Before her, yes;
phrases.notes: From here on it's רב חסדא speaking, reading a hint into the ברייתא's words.

phrases.english: after her, no!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a slave held only by a work-claim can free himself by immersing for freedom
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא implies that slaves who immerse after their owner converts do not go free. That suggests a work-claim is not always cancelled by immersion.

steps.title: רבא: plain immersion versus immersion for freedom
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers: before her conversion, any immersion frees them. After it, an immersion stated explicitly for freedom frees them, but a plain one does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: before her, whether they immersed without saying why or said clearly it was for freedom, they go free. After her, if they said clearly it was for freedom, yes; if they immersed without saying why, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the challenge by splitting the "after her" case into two kinds of immersion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Immersing after her still works if the slaves make clear it is for freedom (מפורש). It fails only when they immerse plainly (סתם), because then it counts as an immersion for slavery. So the ברייתא's "after her, no" applies only to plain immersion, and step 1 still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Plainly, without stating a purpose
Explicitly, clearly stating the purpose

steps.whatToRemember: A slave bought from a גוי can free himself by immersing for freedom. Before his owner converts, any immersion works. After she converts, only an immersion done explicitly for freedom works.

phrases.english: Rava said: Before her,
whether without stated intent or with explicit intent, they go free.
After her: with explicit intent, yes;
without stated intent, no.
phrases.notes: A plain immersion at this point counts as immersing to be a slave, so it doesn't free him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לְפָנֶיהָ, בֵּין בִּסְתָם בֵּין בִּמְפוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: plain immersion versus explicit immersion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא thought that any immersion after her conversion would fail to free the slaves.
steps.terutzMaskana: After her conversion, only a plain immersion fails. An immersion stated explicitly for freedom still frees them.

steps.title: A gentile who sells himself is fully acquired
steps.stepSummary: רב אַוְיָא says the rule that a ישראל buys only the slave's work applies when he buys from a גוי owner. If a גוי sells his own self, the ישראל acquires his body.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אַוְיָא said: This was taught only about someone who buys a slave from a גוי. But if the גוי himself is sold, the ישראל acquires him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אַוְיָא limits the rule from the earlier steps. It covers only a slave bought from a גוי owner, not a גוי who sells himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the reason a ישראל owns only the work was that the גוי owner never owned the body in the first place. When the גוי sells himself, there is no middleman with partial rights. So the ישראל can acquire the body itself.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about... (a phrase that narrows a rule)
One who buys a slave from a גוי owner
His body; also 'himself'
Acquires

phrases.english: Rav Avya said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּלוֹקֵחַ מִן הַגּוֹי,
phrases.english: They taught this only about one who buys from a gentile,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the rule from before: the buyer gets only the slave's work, so immersion frees him.

phrases.english: but a gentile himself — he acquires.
phrases.notes: He means a גוי who sells himself directly to a ישראל. Then the ישראל acquires his body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב אויא לא שנו אלא בלוקח מן הגוי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the rule from steps 1-4 to the case of buying a slave from a גוי owner.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל who buys a slave from a גוי owner gets only his work. A גוי who sells himself to a ישראל is acquired body and all.

steps.title: The verse: you acquire from them
steps.stepSummary: רב אַוְיָא's source is the פסוק 'מהם תקנו'. It teaches that you acquire from them, they do not acquire from you, and they do not acquire from one another.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And also from the children of the settlers who live among you, from them you may acquire.' You acquire from them, but they do not acquire from you, and they do not acquire from one another.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the פסוק that supports רב אַוְיָא. The דרשה reads it as three rules about who can acquire whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They do not acquire from one another' is the key point. A גוי owner never fully owns another גוי's body, so a ישראל who buys from him gets only the work. 'You acquire from them' means a ישראל can acquire a גוי directly. The next steps work out what kind of acquisition this is.

keyTerms.meaning: Settlers; non-Jews living among the Jewish people
You may acquire
From one another

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And also from the children of the settlers
who live among you, from them you may acquire"
You acquire from them,
and they do not acquire from you,
and they do not acquire from one another.

steps.triggerLanguage: דכתיב וגם מבני התושבים הגרים עמכם מהם תקנו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רב אַוְיָא's statement.
steps.raayaObject: רב אַוְיָא's rule that a ישראל can acquire a גוי's body directly, while one גוי cannot fully acquire another.

steps.title: What kind of acquisition does the verse rule out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'they do not acquire from you' refers to. It cannot mean work, because a different פסוק shows a גוי can acquire a ישראל for work.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And they do not acquire from you': for what? If you say for his work, can a גוי not acquire a ישראל for his work? But it is written: 'or to the offshoot of a stranger's family,' and the Master said that 'a stranger's family' means a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of acquisition the דרשה is talking about. It shows that the answer 'for work' does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא 25:47 says a poor ישראל may sell himself to a גוי. A גוי can therefore acquire a ישראל's work. So when the דרשה says 'they do not acquire from you', it must be talking about something else. This prepares the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: For what? (what does this refer to)
The work of his hands; his labor
Is that to say...? (a question showing an idea is not true)
The offshoot of a stranger's family; explained as a גוי

phrases.english: "And they do not acquire from you" — for what?
If you say for his labor —
is that to say a gentile cannot acquire
a Jew for his labor?
But it is written: "or to the offshoot of a stranger's family",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47. That פסוק is about a poor ישראל who sells himself.

phrases.english: and the Master said: "a stranger's family" — this is the gentile!

steps.triggerLanguage: ולא הם קונים מכם למאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the דרשה from step 6 by ruling out one possible meaning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of acquisition does 'they do not acquire from you' rule out: work or body?
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not challenging רב אַוְיָא here. It is clearing away one possible reading so the פסוק can be shown to talk about the body.

steps.title: The verse is about owning the body
steps.stepSummary: So 'they do not acquire from you' must mean the body. Then 'you acquire from them' also means the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about his body? And the Merciful One says: You acquire from them, even his body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the דרשה is talking about owning the body. That supports רב אַוְיָא: a ישראל can acquire a גוי's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both halves of the דרשה are read the same way. A גוי cannot own a ישראל's body or another גוי's body, but a ישראל can own a גוי's body. That is exactly what happens when a גוי sells himself to a ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? (leads to the remaining answer)
The Merciful One; the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אַוְיָא, the פסוק 'מהם תקנו' teaches that a ישראל can own a גוי's body directly. A גוי cannot own another גוי's body, so buying from a גוי owner gives only the work.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not for his body?
And the Merciful One says:
You acquire from them —
even his body.

steps.triggerLanguage: אלא לאו לגופיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer left after step 7 ruled out 'work'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The דרשה is about owning the body, so a ישראל can acquire a גוי's body.

steps.title: Maybe the body is owned only after money and immersion
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא challenges רב אַוְיָא. Maybe the פסוק means the body is owned only through money plus טבילה for slavery, and not through money alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא challenges: Say it means with money and with immersion!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא attacks the proof. He says the פסוק may describe a full acquisition made with money and טבילה together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the body is owned only after the slave's טבילה for slavery, then buying with money alone is not complete. A slave who immersed for freedom before that would still go free, even if he sold himself. Then the פסוק does not prove רב אַוְיָא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Challenges; raises a difficulty
Money
Immersion; here, a slave's immersion for slavery

phrases.english: Rav Acha challenges:
Say: with money and with immersion!
phrases.notes: He means the ישראל owns the body only after paying and also immersing the slave for slavery.

steps.triggerLanguage: פריך רב אחא אימא בכספא ובטבילה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from the פסוק given in steps 6-8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אַוְיָא's proof that money alone gives a ישראל the body of a גוי who sold himself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק can be read as talking about acquisition by money and טבילה together. So it does not prove that money alone acquires the body.

steps.title: The challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits רב אחא's challenge has no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that רב אחא's challenge against רב אַוְיָא stays unanswered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קשיא means the proof for רב אַוְיָא is weakened and no answer is given. It does not always mean his view is completely rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a challenge left without an answer

steps.whatToRemember: רב אַוְיָא's proof from 'מהם תקנו' ends with an unanswered קשיא. The פסוק might mean acquisition by money and טבילה together.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.triggerLanguage: קשיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that the challenge in step 9 has no answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אחא's challenge to רב אַוְיָא is left unanswered, so the proof from the פסוק does not hold.

steps.title: שמואל: Hold the slave firmly in the water
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that when immersing a slave for slavery, the owner must hold him tightly in the water.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: And you need to hold him tightly in the water.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a practical rule about the slave's טבילה: the owner must keep a firm hold on him while he is in the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The firm hold shows that the slave is under his master's control at the moment of immersion. That makes the טבילה count as a טבילה for slavery. The next steps show how this was actually done and why.

keyTerms.meaning: to hold him tightly or firmly
immersion in water, the step that brings a slave into his status

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
And one needs to hold him tightly in the water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, וְצָרִיךְ לְתׇקְפּוֹ בַּמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבא's point in step 4 that a slave can free himself by declaring his immersion is for freedom. שמואל gives the practical way to stop this: the owner holds him tightly in the water.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner must keep a firm hold on the slave during the immersion for slavery.

steps.title: The story of מנימין, רב אשי's slave
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי handed his slave to רבינא and רב אחא בריה דרבא to immerse. He warned them that they would be responsible for him. They put a bridle on the slave's neck, then loosened it and tightened it.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the case of מנימין, רב אשי's slave. רב אשי wanted to immerse him, so he handed him over to רבינא and to רב אחא the son of רבא. He said to them: "Know that I will claim him from you." They put a bridle on his neck, then loosened it and tightened it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real story that shows שמואל's rule being carried out. It is also setting up the next step, which explains each action.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי made the two חכמים responsible: if the slave became free, they would have to pay him back. So they took a firm hold on the slave with a bridle, exactly as שמואל requires. The loosening and tightening look odd here, but the next step explains them.

keyTerms.meaning: the name of רב אשי's slave
I will claim or demand (payment)
a bridle or strap
they loosened
they tightened

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הַאי דְּמִנְיָמִין עַבְדֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Like this case of Minyamin, the slave of Rav Ashi:
he wanted to immerse him.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the round-bracket word; the square-bracket word is the corrected wording. Both mean "to immerse."

phrases.english: He handed him over to them,
to Ravina and to Rav Acha the son of Rava.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לְהוּ: חֲזוֹ דְּמִינַּיְיכוּ קָבָעֵינָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He said to them: See that I will claim him from you,
phrases.notes: He means: if my slave ends up free, I'll hold you two responsible to pay me.

phrases.english: They put a bridle on his neck,
they loosened it and tightened it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הַאי דְּמִנְיָמִין עַבְדֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows שמואל's rule being carried out in a real case.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the slave must be held firmly in the water
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבינא and רב אחא בריה דרבא with רב אשי's slave

steps.title: Why they loosened and tightened the bridle, and the bucket of clay
steps.stepSummary: Loosening the bridle stops anything from blocking the water. Tightening it stops the slave from declaring that he is immersing as a free man. Afterward they gave him a bucket of clay to carry to his master.
steps.simpleTranslation: "They loosened it" so there would be nothing blocking the water. "They tightened it" so he could not jump ahead and say to them: "I am immersing for the sake of a free man." As he lifted his head out of the water, they put a bucket of clay on his head. They said to him: "Go, bring it to your master's house."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each step of the bridle was done, and then finishes the story with the bucket of clay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two needs pulled in opposite directions. The טבילה must have no חציצה (nothing between the body and the water), so the bridle had to be loose. But the slave also had to stay under the master's control, so he could not declare he was immersing to become free. Giving him a slave's job as soon as he came out showed that he was still a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: something blocking the water from touching the body, which ruins a טבילה
to jump ahead, to act first
a free man
a bucket of clay
your master

steps.whatToRemember: The bridle was loosened so the טבילה would be valid, and tightened so the slave could not declare himself free. The bucket of clay showed he was still a slave.
steps.confusionAlert: The loosening and the tightening are not a contradiction. Each one solves a different problem: the first prevents a חציצה, and the second keeps the master in control.

phrases.english: "They loosened it":
so that there would not be anything blocking.
"They tightened it":

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לַקְדֵּים וְלֵימָא לְהוּ:
phrases.english: so that he would not jump ahead and say to them:
I am immersing for the sake of a free man.
As he lifted his head out of the water,
they placed a bucket of clay on his head

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: זִיל אַמְטִי לְבֵי מָרָךְ.
phrases.english: and said to him: Go, bring it to your master's house.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַרְפּוֹ לֵיהּ כִּי הֵיכִי דְּלָא לֶהֱוֵי חֲצִיצָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the actions described in the story and completes it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loosening prevents a חציצה; tightening keeps the slave from declaring himself free; the work right afterward shows he is still a slave.

steps.title: רב פפא's question: people whose head-tax was paid for them
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks רבא about the house of פפא בר אבא, who paid poor people's head-tax and then made them work. When those people go free, do they need a document of freedom?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: "Has the master seen those people of the house of פפא בר אבא? They give money for people's head-tax, and then make those people work for them. When these people go out, do they need a document of freedom, or not?"
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. רב פפא asks whether people who were taken over by paying their tax need a גט שחרור when they leave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is really this: what exactly did paying the tax buy? If it bought the person's body as a slave, he needs a document of freedom to leave. If it only bought his work, he can leave without one.

keyTerms.meaning: head-tax, a tax on each person
they make them work for them, they enslave them
a document of freedom (גט שחרור)
they go out, they go free

steps.whyThisMatters: It ties back to the earlier debate (steps 6–10) about whether one can acquire a person's body or only his work.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:

phrases.aramaic: חֲזִי מָר הָנֵי דְּבֵי פָּפָּא בַּר אַבָּא,
phrases.english: Has the master seen those of the house of Pappa bar Abba,
who give money on behalf of people for their head-tax
and then make them work for them?
When they go free,
do they need a document of freedom, or not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְרָבָא: חֲזִי מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the slave's immersion to a new practical case about people taken over by paying their tax.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether people taken over by paying their head-tax need a גט שחרור when they leave, which depends on whether their body or only their work was acquired.

steps.title: רבא answers: the king's decree truly makes them slaves
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב פפא using רב ששת's teaching. The king owns the bodies of everyone in his kingdom, so his rule that a non-payer belongs to whoever pays his tax makes those poor people real slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: If I were dead, I could not have told you this. This is what רב ששת said: The slavery papers of these people are kept in the king's treasury. And the king said: Whoever does not pay the head-tax is enslaved to whoever pays the head-tax for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from Step 14. He quotes רב ששת to show that the poor people who were made to work really became slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether the work arrangement was only a debt deal or true slavery. רב ששת teaches that the king already owns everyone in the kingdom, as if their slavery papers sit in his treasury. So when the king hands a non-payer over to the person who paid, that person becomes a real owner, and the slave would need a document of freedom to go free.

keyTerms.meaning: If I were dead (literally 'if I were lying down')
A document of ownership or slavery
The king's treasury, where official papers are kept
Head-tax, a tax every person must pay
Becomes enslaved or bound to someone

steps.whatToRemember: Because the king owns his subjects, his decree truly makes a non-payer the slave of the one who paid the tax. So these people need a document of freedom when they are set free.
steps.confusionAlert: The text never says 'yes, they need a document.' That answer comes from רב ששת's rule. If they are real slaves, they need a real release.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבא answering רב פפא's question from Step 14.

phrases.english: If I were dead,
I could not tell you this matter.
phrases.notes: He means: it's good you asked me while I'm alive, because I know the answer.

phrases.english: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
The slavery documents of these people
are kept in the king's treasury,
phrases.notes: In other words, the king owns all his subjects as if they were his slaves.

phrases.english: and the king said:
Whoever does not pay the head-tax
is enslaved to whoever pays the head-tax.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִיכּוֹ שְׁכֵיבִי לָא אֲמַרִי לְכוּ הָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's question from Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether people enslaved for unpaid head-tax need a document of freedom.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The king owns his subjects, so his decree makes them full slaves of the one who paid.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבא sees problems in גבלא and stays silent
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבא visited גבלא. He saw Jewish women pregnant from converts who had circumcised but not immersed, Jews drinking wine that gentiles had poured, and Jews eating lupines cooked by gentiles. He said nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא came to גבלא. He saw Jewish women who became pregnant from converts who were circumcised but did not immerse. He saw Jewish wine that gentiles mixed and Jews drank. He saw lupines that gentiles cooked and Jews ate. He said nothing at all to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story. It sets up three problems that רבי יוחנן will respond to in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three things is a possible problem. The converts' conversion may not be finished, the wine may be forbidden because gentiles handled it, and the food may be forbidden because gentiles cooked it. רבי חייא בר אבא's silence sets up the question of what he should have done.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come to a place
גבלא, a place name
Were circumcised but did not immerse in a מקוה
Mix or pour wine (often diluting it with water)
Lupines, a bitter bean that must be cooked to be eaten

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba happened to come to Gavla.
He saw Jewish women
who became pregnant from converts
who were circumcised but did not immerse,
and he saw wine belonging to Jews
that gentiles mixed and Jews drank,
and he saw lupines
that gentiles cooked and Jews ate,
and he did not say anything at all to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אִיקְּלַע לְגַבְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new story, linked to the earlier discussion of טבילה and conversion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up the story: three problems in גבלא, and רבי חייא בר אבא stays silent.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן orders a public announcement
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells רבי חייא בר אבא to announce that the children are ממזרים, the wine is forbidden as יין נסך, and the lupines are forbidden as בישולי גוים, because the people there are not learned in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבי יוחנן. רבי יוחנן said to him: Go and announce about their children that they are ממזרים, about their wine that it is forbidden as יין נסך, and about their lupines that they are forbidden as בישולי גוים, because they are not people of Torah.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן reacts to the story. He tells רבי חייא בר אבא that he should not stay silent, and he should make a public announcement about all three problems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן gives a ruling for each of the three problems. He adds a reason: the people of גבלא are not learned in Torah, so they need clear and strict warnings. The next steps explain why the children are called ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: Announce publicly
A child from a forbidden union, who may not marry a regular Jew
Wine poured for idol worship; also wine handled by a gentile, which is forbidden
Food cooked by a gentile, which the חכמים forbade
People who are learned in Torah

phrases.english: He came before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to him: Go and announce
about their children that they are mamzerim,
and about their wine, because of yayin nesech,
and about their lupines, because of food cooked by gentiles,
because they are not people of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: צֵא וְהַכְרֵז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן responds to the three problems seen in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Announce that the children are ממזרים, the wine is יין נסך, and the lupines are בישולי גוים.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule: no convert without immersion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that calling the children ממזרים follows רבי יוחנן's own view. A person is not a convert until he has both had מילה and done טבילה, so a convert who did not immerse is still a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About their children being ממזרים: רבי יוחנן follows his own reasoning. רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A person is never a convert until he is circumcised and immerses. And since he did not immerse, he is a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to explain why רבי יוחנן called the children ממזרים. This step gives the first half of the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that conversion needs both מילה and טבילה. The men in גבלא were circumcised but never immersed, so in הלכה they were still גוים. The next step adds the second half of the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning, consistent with his other rulings
A person is never a convert
Until he is circumcised and immerses

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the circumcision made them half-Jewish. Without טבילה, רבי יוחנן says the person is still fully a גוי.

phrases.english: About their children being mamzerim —
Rabbi Yochanan follows his own reasoning.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: For Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
A person is never a convert
until he is circumcised and immerses.
And since he did not immerse, he is a gentile.
phrases.notes: This is talking about the men of גבלא from Step 16.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל בְּנֵיהֶן שֶׁהֵם מַמְזֵרִים — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first ruling of Step 17 by pointing to another teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person is not a convert until he has both מילה and טבילה; without טבילה he is still a גוי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule: a גוי's child from a Jewish woman is a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second teaching of רבי יוחנן: when a גוי or an עבד has relations with a Jewish woman, the child is a ממזר. Together with the previous step, this explains why the children in גבלא are ממזרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A גוי or an עבד who has relations with a Jewish woman — the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of the reason for רבי יוחנן's ruling about the children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed that the fathers in גבלא were still גוים. This step adds that a child born to a Jewish woman from a גוי is a ממזר. Put the two together, and the children of those women are ממזרים, just as רבי יוחנן said.

keyTerms.meaning: Who has relations with
A Jewish woman
The child born from the union

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's ruling rests on two of his teachings: (1) without טבילה, a convert is still a גוי; (2) the child of a גוי and a Jewish woman is a ממזר. So the children in גבלא are ממזרים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a single practical ruling can come from combining two separate rules of the same אמורא.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: And Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: A gentile or a slave who has relations with a Jewish woman —
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the second teaching that completes the explanation started in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The child of a גוי or עבד and a Jewish woman is a ממזר.

steps.title: Why the wine of גבלא is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the wine ban in גבלא is a protective fence, based on the saying that a נזיר is told to go far around a vineyard.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wine was declared forbidden as יין נסך because of the saying: 'Go, go, we tell the נזיר, go around and around, and do not come near the vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining רבי יוחנן's announcements from step 17. Now it explains the second one, about the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is only forbidden to eat grape products, yet he is told to keep away from the vineyard itself so he won't slip. In the same way, wine that a גוי only poured is forbidden as a fence, so people stay far from real idol-worship wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for idol worship; here, wine forbidden because a גוי handled it
A נזיר, a person who vowed to stay away from grape products
Go around, go around; keep your distance
Vineyard

phrases.english: And concerning their wine, that it is forbidden as idol-worship wine:
this is because of the saying: "Go, go, we say to the nazirite,
go around, go around, do not come near the vineyard."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל יֵינָם מִשּׁוּם יֵין נֶסֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining the ממזרים in steps 18-19, the גמרא moves to the second announcement, the wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine poured by a גוי is forbidden as a protective fence, just as a נזיר is told to keep away from a vineyard.

steps.title: Why the lupines of גבלא are forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the lupines were forbidden as בישולי גוים because the people of גבלא were not learned in Torah.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lupines were declared forbidden as food cooked by גוים because the people were not בני תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי יוחנן's third announcement, about the lupines. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given is about the people, not the food: they are not learned in Torah. That wording hints that for learned people the lupines might be allowed, and the גמרא will question this right away.

keyTerms.meaning: Lupine, a bitter bean that must be cooked before eating
Food cooked by גוים, which the חכמים forbade
People learned in Torah

phrases.english: And concerning their lupines, that they are forbidden as food cooked by gentiles:
this is because they are not people of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַל תּוֹרְמוֹסָן מִשּׁוּם בִּשּׁוּלֵי גוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of explanations, moving from the wine to the lupines.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lupine ban in גבלא was given because the people were not learned in Torah.

steps.title: But lupines should be forbidden for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: is it really allowed for learned people? רב said that only food eaten raw is free of בישולי גוים, and lupines are not eaten raw, so they should be forbidden for everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean learned people may eat them? But רב שמואל בר רב יצחק said in the name of רב: anything eaten raw is not included in בישולי גוים. A lupine is not eaten raw, so it is included!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason from the last step. It argues that lupines should be forbidden to everyone, learned or not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רב's rule, the test is whether a food can be eaten raw. Lupines can't be eaten raw, so cooked lupines from a גוי are fully forbidden. Then why did רבי יוחנן blame only the people's lack of learning?

keyTerms.meaning: Does that mean it is permitted?
As it is, raw
But didn't he say?

phrases.english: Does that mean that for people of Torah it is permitted?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak say in the name of Rav:
Anything that is eaten as it is, raw,
is not subject to the ban on food cooked by gentiles.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תּוֹרְמוֹס אֵינוֹ נֶאֱכָל כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא חַי,
phrases.english: And a lupine is not eaten as it is, raw,
so it is subject to the ban on food cooked by gentiles!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא בְּנֵי תוֹרָה שְׁרֵי? וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks what step 21 implies, that learned people may eat the lupines.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that lupines cooked by a גוי are allowed for בני תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's rule exempts only foods eaten raw. Lupines are not eaten raw, so they are fully included in בישולי גוים for everyone.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן follows the other version of רב's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן holds like a different version of רב's rule: only foods fit for a king's table are included. Lupines are not, so the ban is only a fence for people who aren't learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds like the other version, where רב said: anything not served on a king's table to eat with bread is not included in בישולי גוים. So the only reason for the ban is that they are not learned, and for learned people it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It says רב's rule was reported in two versions, and רבי יוחנן follows the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second version the test is how important a food is, not whether it can be eaten raw. A simple food like lupines is not included at all. So רבי יוחנן's ban was only a fence for people who might become careless.

keyTerms.meaning: The other version of a teaching
The table of kings; an important, fancy food
He holds, he is of the opinion
Bread

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of רב's rule on בישולי גוים: food eaten raw is not included, or food not served at a king's table is not included. רבי יוחנן follows the second, so lupines are allowed to learned people.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּאִידַּךְ לִישָּׁנָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds like the other version,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר רַב יִצְחָק מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said in the name of Rav:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין עוֹלֶה עַל שׁוּלְחַן מְלָכִים
phrases.english: Anything that is not served on the table of kings
to eat bread with it
is not subject to the ban on food cooked by gentiles,
and the reason for the ban is that they are not people of Torah,
but for people of Torah it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן כְּאִידַּךְ לִישָּׁנָא סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by pointing to a different version of רב's rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different version of the cited teaching (אידך לישנא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רב's rule depends on whether a food is eaten raw, which would forbid lupines for everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן follows the version that depends on whether the food is fit for a king's table. Lupines are not included, so the ban is only a fence for the unlearned.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: מילה alone makes a convert
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins: רבי אליעזר says a convert who had מילה but no טבילה is a גר, because our forefathers had מילה without טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: a convert who had מילה but no טבילה — רבי אליעזר says he is a convert, because we found that our forefathers had מילה but no טבילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about the point from step 18, what makes someone a convert. This is the first of three opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns from our forefathers at יציאת מצרים, who had מילה but, in his view, no טבילה. So for him מילה alone is enough. This differs from רבי יוחנן's view in step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: A convert to Judaism
Was circumcised
Immersed in a מקוה
Our forefathers

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A convert who was circumcised but did not immerse,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: this is a convert,
for so we found with our forefathers
phrases.notes: He means the Jewish men when they left מצרים.

phrases.english: that they were circumcised but did not immerse.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גֵּר שֶׁמָּל וְלֹא טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section with a ברייתא about the conversion rule mentioned in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר: מילה without טבילה makes a person a גר.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: טבילה alone makes a convert
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says a convert who had טבילה but no מילה is a גר, because our foremothers had טבילה and of course no מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who immersed but was not circumcised — רבי יהושע says he is a convert, because we found that our foremothers immersed and were not circumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the second opinion. רבי יהושע says טבילה alone is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע learns from the women at that time, who became Jewish through טבילה alone, since women have no מילה. So for him a male convert also becomes a גר through טבילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our foremothers, the women of that generation
This one is

phrases.english: One who immersed but was not circumcised,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: הֲרֵי זֶה גֵּר,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: this is a convert,
for so we found with the foremothers
that they immersed and were not circumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָבַל וְלֹא מָל, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view: טבילה alone, instead of מילה alone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע: טבילה without מילה makes a person a גר.

steps.title: The חכמים: a convert needs both מילה and טבילה
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that whichever one is missing, the person is not a convert until he has both מילה and טבילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: whether he immersed and was not circumcised, or was circumcised and did not immerse, he is not a convert until he is circumcised and immerses.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the third opinion. The חכמים require both steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים reject both one-step views. A man must have both מילה and טבילה to become a גר. This is the view רבי יוחנן used in step 18 to call the children of גבלא ממזרים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion
Until he is circumcised and immerses

steps.whatToRemember: Three views: רבי אליעזר says מילה alone is enough, רבי יהושע says טבילה alone is enough, and the חכמים require both. רבי יוחנן's rule in step 18 matches the חכמים.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the names. רבי אליעזר is the one who learns from the forefathers (מילה). רבי יהושע is the one who learns from the foremothers (טבילה).
steps.whyThisMatters: The חכמים's view matches רבי יוחנן's rule in step 18. A man who had only מילה is still a גוי, so his children from a Jewish woman are ממזרים, as רבי יוחנן ruled about גבלא.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:

phrases.aramaic: טָבַל וְלֹא מָל, מָל וְלֹא טָבַל —
phrases.english: Whether he immersed but was not circumcised, or was circumcised but did not immerse,
he is not a convert until he is circumcised and immerses.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: טָבַל וְלֹא מָל, מָל וְלֹא טָבַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע and requires both steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A man becomes a גר only after both מילה and טבילה.

steps.title: Why doesn't each תנא learn from both the forefathers and the foremothers?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges both רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר for each using only one source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יהושע also learn from the forefathers, and let רבי אליעזר also learn from the foremothers!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why each תנא only looked at one group. רבי יהושע could have learned from the אבות, and רבי אליעזר could have learned from the אמהות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learned from the אבות that מילה alone is enough. רבי יהושע learned from the אמהות that טבילה alone is enough. Each could also have learned from the other group, so each should accept both one-step paths: רבי יהושע should also accept מילה alone, and רבי אליעזר should also accept טבילה alone.

keyTerms.meaning: Let him learn (derive)
Forefathers
Foremothers

phrases.english: But let Rabbi Yehoshua also learn from the forefathers,
phrases.notes: The forefathers had מילה without טבילה, which is רבי אליעזר's source from step 24.

phrases.english: and let Rabbi Eliezer also learn from the foremothers!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ נָמֵי נֵילַף מֵאָבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the sources used by the תנאים in the ברייתא from steps 24-26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The way רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע each pick only one source.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both groups are available as models for conversion, so each תנא should take both into account.

steps.title: A suggested answer: you can't learn the possible from the impossible
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי אליעזר doesn't learn from the אמהות because it was impossible for women to have מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: one cannot learn the possible from the impossible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer, but it is only a suggestion and is about to be tested. Women could never have מילה, so maybe that case can't teach anything about men, who can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'אין דנין אפשר משאי אפשר' says you cannot copy a law from a case where the action was impossible to a case where it is possible. The אמהות skipped מילה only because they could not have it, so that would not teach that men may skip it. This would explain why רבי אליעזר ignores the אמהות.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)
One cannot learn the possible from the impossible

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. וכי תימא brings an idea that the גמרא is about to knock down.

phrases.english: And if you would say,
one cannot learn the possible from the impossible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of רבי אליעזר against the question in step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits which sources may be used, based on a general rule of learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The אמהות should teach that מילה is not needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אמהות never could have מילה, so they teach nothing about men.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר learns the later פסח from the פסח in Egypt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי אליעזר learning the yearly פסח from the פסח in מצרים, where using sanctified animals was impossible.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is taught: רבי אליעזר says: How do we know the yearly פסח comes only from non-sacred animals? פסח is said about מצרים and פסח is said about later generations. Just as the פסח in מצרים came only from non-sacred animals, so too the later פסח comes only from non-sacred animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the suggestion from step 28. It quotes a ברייתא where רבי אליעזר himself learns from the פסח in מצרים, where something was impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מצרים there was no קדושה of animals yet, so the פסח could only come from חולין. Even so, רבי אליעזר learns from it that the yearly פסח must also come from חולין, even though later it would be possible to use sanctified animals. So it looks like he does learn the possible from the impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: The yearly פסח brought in all later generations
The פסח brought in Egypt before leaving
Non-sacred (ordinary) animals

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
From where do we know about the Pesach of the generations
that it comes only from non-sacred animals?
Pesach is said about Egypt,
and Pesach is said about the generations.
Just as the Pesach stated about Egypt
came only from non-sacred animals,
so too the Pesach stated for the generations
comes only from non-sacred animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the suggested answer of step 28 with a source from רבי אליעזר himself.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי אליעזר holds you cannot learn the possible from the impossible.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the case of פסח, רבי אליעזר learns from the פסח in מצרים, where sanctified animals were impossible.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר tells רבי עקיבא that an impossible case is still a great proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא objects with the rule from step 28, and רבי אליעזר answers that he still learns from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: Can one learn the possible from the impossible? He answered: Even though it was impossible, it is a great proof and we learn from it. Rather...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא raises the same rule that step 28 suggested, and רבי אליעזר openly rejects it. This proves the suggestion in step 28 is wrong, and the last word אלא sets up a new answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר clearly says that a case where something was impossible can still teach a law. So he could have learned from the אמהות, and the question of step 27 comes back. The גמרא therefore has to explain the ברייתא in a new way.

keyTerms.meaning: But can one learn? (a challenge)
A great proof
Rather (opens a new approach)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר holds that even an impossible case can teach a law, so 'אין דנין אפשר משאי אפשר' cannot explain why he ignores the אמהות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
But can one learn the possible from the impossible?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר —
phrases.english: He said to him: Even though it was impossible,
it is a great proof, and we learn from it.
Rather...
phrases.notes: The גמרא is starting a brand-new answer here; the rest of it comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: וְכִי דָּנִין אֶפְשָׁר מִשֶּׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 29 and seals the rejection of step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר does learn the possible from the impossible.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אליעזר's reply to רבי עקיבא in the ברייתא about the פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the suggested answer fails, the question of step 27 stands again, and the גמרא must reread the ברייתא about converts.
